environment.description: Rails 7 application deployed on AWS ECS Fargate behind an Application Load Balancer. The ALB is configured to forward WebSocket upgrade requests on /cable directly to the Puma backend on port 3000. The ALB target group has stickiness enabled for WebSocket connections. No additional authentication layer exists between the ALB and the application. The allowed_request_origins regex permits any subdomain of example.com, and an attacker who controls a subdomain (e.g., via dangling DNS/subdomain takeover on attacker.example.com) can set a matching Origin header.

config.alb_listener_rules: Forward /cable to target group, WebSocket upgrade allowed
config.network: ALB public-facing, port 443 -> target group port 3000
config.dns: Wildcard subdomain delegation with multiple CNAME records, some dangling
